To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the severity of coronary dysfunction increases with the severity of insulin resistance and carbohydrate intolerance.

the functional abnormalities of coronary circulatory function that occur in states of insulin-resistance are progressive, beginning in insulin-resistant states without carbohydrate intolerance and progressing in magnitude with the severity of the metabolic abnormality.
progressively worsening functional coronary circulary abnormalities of nitric-oxide-mediated, endothelium dependent vasomotion occur over the full spectrum from insulin resistance to diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis and treatment of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.
the role of the coronary circulation in the development of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in diabetes.
the study of insulin resistance, impaired glucose tolerance, and type 2 diabetes in the context of coronary vascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

insulin resistance and diabetes are associated with progressive coronary circulatory dysfunction that is characterized by impaired endothelium-dependent and total vasodilatory function, and that these functional abnormalities are present before the development of overt carbohydrate intolerance.
the coronary circulation is abnormal in the presence of insulin resistance, and that this abnormality worsens with increasing severity of the metabolic syndrome.
insulin resistance and diabetes are associated with progressive abnormalities in the coronary vasculature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelium is the earliest target for the effects of insulin resistance, which may be the first step in the pathogenesis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

endothelial dysfunction is the first step in the pathophysiology of coronary circulatory dysfunction in insulin resistance, and that it is associated with an accelerated progression toward more advanced stages of insulin resistance.

endothelium-dependent, nitric oxide-mediated vasomotion is the first functional abnormality in the coronary circulation to occur with the development of insulin resistance, which is followed by a more global impairment of total coronary vasodilator function with the progression to diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelium is dysfunctional in insulin resistance.
endothelium-dependent, nitric oxide–dependent, vasomotion is impaired early in the course of insulin resistance and is further impaired with the development of diabetes.

the coronary circulatory dysfunction is not only present in patients with diabetes, but also in patients with insulin resistance, and that the coronary circulation is affected early in the disease process, before the development of diabetes.
